title: Square root covariance update error and stability

items.title: An explicit rational envelope for the scaled Householder QR error
items.statement: Let $q\ge n\ge1$, $u>0$, and let $\kappa_q$ be the local scaled-Householder coefficient of [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]] at active row dimension $q$. Set $$ \beta_{q,n}=(1+\kappa_q)^n-1,\qquad C_{q,n}=200qn. $$ If $C_{q,n}u<1$, then $$ \beta_{q,n}\le\eta_{q,n}:=\frac{C_{q,n}u}{1-C_{q,n}u}. $$ Thus the QR backward-error factor can be bounded by the stated rational dimension-dependent expression in this precision range.

items.title: A factor perturbation gives an explicit Gram-matrix error
items.statement: Let $G,E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and set $\widehat G=G+E$. Then $$ \|\widehat G\widehat G^T-GG^T\|_F \le 2\|G\|_F\|E\|_F+\|E\|_F^2. $$ The estimate is valid for all ranks, including $G=0$ and rank-deficient factors.

items.statement: Let $P^-=L^- (L^-)^T$ and $R=L_RL_R^T$, with real factors of arbitrary rank. items.title: QR prediction preserves the canonical covariance factor
items.statement: Let $P=LL^T$ with $L\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}$ and let $Q=L_Q L_Q^T$ with $L_Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}$, where zero columns and rank deficiency are allowed. For any real $F\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, form $G=[FL\;L_Q]$ and append zero columns if needed so that the transpose has at least $n$ rows. In exact arithmetic, if $G^T=UR$ is a reduced QR factorization with $U^TU=I$, then $L^-:=R^T$ satisfies $$ L^-(L^-)^T=FPF^T+Q. $$

items.statement: Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_k$ for $0\le k\le T$, and positive observation dimensions $p_k$ for $1\le k\le T$. Inputs are real finite matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_{k-1}}$, $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, observation vectors $y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$, and an initial mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$. items.title: Product and Householder QR errors bound the represented joint covariance
items.statement: Let $G\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, with $q\ge n$, be an exact prediction or measurement prearray. Let $\widehat G$ be its computed version and assume $$ \|\widehat G-G\|_F\le e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}}, $$ where $e_{\mathrm{form}},e_{\mathrm{in}}\ge0$, $e_{\mathrm{form}}$ bounds rounded products used to form the array, and $e_{\mathrm{in}}$ bounds separately specified input-factor uncertainty. items.title: The square-root Kalman procedure returns a finite status
items.statement: For every finite admissible input to [[alg-finite-budget-square-root-kalman-filter]] with finite state and observation dimensions, the procedure returns after finitely many arithmetic operations. For $T>0$ its outcome is one of success, range-failure, or innovation-factorization-failure. This is a termination and status result only; it asserts neither that the numerical factorization succeeds nor that an error bound holds.

items.title: The square-root filter has an explicit conditioned finite-horizon error bound
items.statement: Fix a finite horizon $T$ and let $(m_{k|k},P_{k|k})$ and $(m_k^-,P_k^-)$ be the exact real-arithmetic prediction and update recursions of [[alg-kalman-filter]]. Let $$ S_k=H_kP_k^-H_k^T+R_k,\qquad B_k=P_k^-H_k^T,\qquad v_k=y_k-H_km_k^-. $$ Suppose each innovation has a certified lower bound $$ x^TS_kx\ge\mu_k\|x\|_2^2\quad(x\in\mathbb R^{p_k}),\qquad \mu_k>0. $$ Let the procedure [[alg-finite-budget-square-root-kalman-filter]] output represented covariances $\widehat P_{k|k}=\widehat L_{k|k}\widehat L_{k|k}^T$ and means $\widehat m_{k|k}$. title: Square root covariance update error and stability — Examples

items.title: A nonzero prearray perturbation changes the posterior but keeps its factor product PSD
items.statement: Use a scalar state and observation with $P^-=R=H=1$. The exact measurement prearray is $$ Z=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}. $$ For the perturbation calculation take $$ E=\begin{bmatrix}0&1/10\\0&0\end{bmatrix}, \qquad \widehat Z=Z+E. $$ This is a mathematical backward-perturbation example; it does not assert that a particular floating-point QR produces this exact $E$.

items.title: A rounded subtractive covariance update can become indefinite
items.statement: Use binary floating-point arithmetic with precision $p=24$, round-to-nearest ties-to-even, and a normal exponent range containing the values below. Let $$ c=1-2^{-24},\qquad P^-=\begin{bmatrix}1&c\\c&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad H=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad R=2^{-22}. $$ Compute $B= P^-H^T$, then $S=HB+R$, then $K=B/S$, and finally $P_{\rm sub}=P^- - (KS)K^T$, rounding every displayed operation in the specified format.

items.title: A singular prior factor with a positive innovation remains admissible
items.statement: Take one state and one observation, one update step, $m_0=2$, $F=H=1$, $y=7$, and factors $L_0=L_Q=0$, $L_R=1$. The initial, process, and measurement covariances are $P_0=Q=0$ and $R=1$.

items.title: A nearly noiseless weakly scaled observation amplifies innovation-solve residual
items.statement: Take a scalar predicted variance $P^-=1$, observation coefficient $H=10^{-3}$, and measurement variance $R=10^{-12}$. For innovation $v=1$, suppose the computed triangular solve has residual $L_{11}\widehat z-v=10^{-9}$, with no other mean-update error.
